title: Epidemic and emerging disease alerts in the Pacific as of 25 August 2026 - ReliefWeb

analysis.time: Published 25 August 2026; event dates range from 1 January 2026 to 21 August 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: American Samoa (territory of the United States), Marshall Islands (Majuro Atoll), New Caledonia, Samoa, Vanuatu (South-West Efate Island, Shefa Province), Wallis and Futuna.
analysis.event: Multiple Pacific territories reported dengue outbreaks or elevated transmission with serotype-specific alerts: American Samoa (DENV-1 & DENV-2 blue alert), Marshall Islands (DENV-? red alert), Samoa (DENV-1 & DENV-2 blue alert), Vanuatu (DENV-1 red alert), Wallis and Futuna (DENV-1 red alert). New Caledonia declared the dengue epidemic over on 16 August 2026.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: American Samoa: 1,044 laboratory-confirmed cases since outbreak start; weekly counts low (2–3 cases in EpiWeeks 30–32). Marshall Islands: 8 confirmed cases, 15 negative, no deaths; outbreak declared 21 August 2026. New Caledonia: 2,235 cases (2,028 locally acquired), 80 hospitalisations, 4 deaths (1 co-infected with leptospirosis, 3 with comorbidities); DENV-1 only; epidemic declared over. Samoa: 22 new cases in EpiWeek 32 (47% increase), 3 laboratory-confirmed; cumulative 20,157 clinically diagnosed and 5,536 laboratory-confirmed cases since 1 January 2025, 9 deaths; DENV-1 (52%) and DENV-2 (48%) circulating.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: American Samoa: Weekly counts declining since January 2026 peak; cases concentrated in 11–20-year age groups; blue alert remains. Marshall Islands: Active outbreak response coordinated under EpiNet with National Disaster Council; active case finding, vector control, laboratory referral, and public health messaging; larvicide applied around residences; serotyping pending. New Caledonia: Epidemic declared over; low-level circulation persists; Wolbachia intervention in Greater Nouméa. Samoa: Blue alert remains; both serotypes circulating; 73% of cases under 15 years.

analysis.brief_en: As of 25 August 2026, multiple Pacific territories reported ongoing or elevated dengue activity with serotype-specific alerts. American Samoa recorded 1,044 laboratory-confirmed cases since the start of its outbreak, with weekly counts now low and concentrated among adolescents and young adults. The Marshall Islands declared an active dengue fever outbreak on 21 August after identifying eight confirmed cases and initiating coordinated response measures including active case finding and vector control. New Caledonia declared its dengue epidemic over on 16 August, having reported 2,235 cases and four deaths since January, with DENV-1 as the sole circulating serotype. Samoa saw a 47% weekly increase in new cases, while Vanuatu’s South-West Efate outbreak reached 91 confirmed cases with no severe outcomes. Wallis and Futuna reported 70 confirmed or probable cases, with transmission focused in Futuna. Serotype data indicate DENV-1 predominance in most locations, with DENV-2 co-circulating in Samoa.
